title: SCQA builder
prompt: Write two different SCQA formulations from the same context.
context: The Olympics has historically been one of the most unifying global events. However, recent games have struggled to capture the same cultural impact and collective attention. The challenge is understanding why the Games are losing their hold on people and what can be done to win it back.

practiceScenarios.title: A project is falling behind
practiceScenarios.context: A cross-functional team committed to launching a customer portal in six weeks. Two important technical dependencies are now delayed, but leadership still expects the original launch date.

sampleAnswer.s: The cross-functional team committed to launching a customer portal in six weeks, and leadership is planning around that date.
sampleAnswer.c: Two critical technical dependencies are delayed, which puts the original scope and launch date at risk.
sampleAnswer.q: How should the team adjust the plan to protect the most important customer and business outcomes?
sampleAnswer.a: The team should keep the launch date but reduce the first release to the essential customer journey, move dependent features into a scheduled second release, and ask leadership to approve the revised scope this week.

practiceScenarios.title: Customers are not using a new service
practiceScenarios.context: A company launched a new support service three months ago. Customer awareness is high, but very few customers have tried it and the team does not know why.

sampleAnswer.s: The company launched a new support service three months ago and has already made most target customers aware of it.
sampleAnswer.c: Trial remains low despite strong awareness, and the team does not know whether the barrier is relevance, trust, price, or the signup experience.
sampleAnswer.q: What is preventing interested customers from trying the service?
sampleAnswer.a: The team should interview aware non-users, review where customers leave the signup process, and test a simpler first-use offer before investing in more promotion.

practiceScenarios.title: Household responsibilities feel uneven
practiceScenarios.context: Three people share a home and agreed to divide the weekly chores. One person now handles most of the cleaning and reminders, while the others believe the arrangement is fair.

sampleAnswer.s: Three people share a home and agreed that everyone would contribute to the weekly chores.
sampleAnswer.c: One person now does most of the cleaning and reminding, while the others believe the current arrangement is balanced.
sampleAnswer.q: How can the household divide responsibilities in a way that is clear and fair to everyone?
sampleAnswer.a: The household should list the recurring chores, agree on the effort each one requires, assign named owners on a rotating schedule, and review the arrangement after two weeks.

practiceScenarios.title: Friends cannot agree on a group trip
practiceScenarios.context: Five friends want to take a three-day trip together. They have different budgets, preferred activities, and available weekends, and every proposed plan leaves someone out.

sampleAnswer.s: Five friends want to take a three-day trip together and are willing to plan around the needs of the group.
sampleAnswer.c: Their budgets, interests, and available weekends differ enough that each proposed plan excludes at least one person.
sampleAnswer.q: How can the group choose a trip that everyone can afford and attend without restarting the discussion each time?
sampleAnswer.a: The group should first agree on a maximum budget and two possible weekends, remove destinations that fail either condition, and then vote on the remaining options using each person's top activity as a preference rather than a requirement.

practiceScenarios.title: A school group project is off track
practiceScenarios.context: Four students have ten days to finish a group presentation. Two students have completed their sections, one keeps changing the main idea, and one has not submitted any work.

sampleAnswer.s: Four students have ten days to complete one group presentation, and two sections are already drafted.
sampleAnswer.c: The main idea keeps changing and one student has not contributed, putting the quality and deadline at risk.
sampleAnswer.q: How should the group organize the remaining work so it submits one clear presentation on time?
sampleAnswer.a: The group should agree on one main idea today, assign each unfinished section to a named student with a two-day deadline, combine the slides in one file, and reserve the final three days for editing and rehearsal.

sampleAnswers.s: The Olympics remains one of the world's most recognizable sports properties, with unmatched history, global reach, athlete prestige, and symbolic power.
sampleAnswers.c: But recognition is no longer converting into cultural relevance. Audiences now encounter the Games through fragmented feeds, isolated clips, louder political and commercial signals, and fewer shared rituals, so the Olympics risks feeling less like a rare global moment and more like another stream of optional content.
sampleAnswers.q: How can LA 2028 convert the Olympics' unmatched recognition into renewed cultural relevance without chasing trends, weakening neutrality, or diluting the brand?
sampleAnswers.a: LA 2028 should rebuild Olympic relevance by treating the Games as a coherent cultural ritual, not just a content property: design shared appointment moments, build athlete-led story arcs that make stakes accumulate over time, and enforce a disciplined editorial and partner system that protects prestige, neutrality, and meaning across every channel.

sampleAnswers.s: The Olympics remains one of the world's most recognizable sports properties, with unmatched history, global reach, athlete prestige, and symbolic power.
sampleAnswers.c: But recognition is no longer converting into cultural relevance. Audiences now encounter the Games through fragmented feeds, isolated clips, louder political and commercial signals, and fewer shared rituals, so the Olympics risks feeling less like a rare global moment and more like another stream of optional content.
sampleAnswers.q: Rather than trying to win back every audience at once, which single audience should LA 2028 prioritize to rebuild the Olympics' cultural relevance fastest?
sampleAnswers.a: LA 2028 should prioritize younger, casual sports fans over legacy loyalists: this group is the most reachable through short-form and creator-led content, the most likely to turn single moments into recurring attention, and the audience whose renewed engagement would most convincingly signal that the Games still matter culturally.
